post.description:
Calls `POST /admin/drain` on one instance: its `/readyz` starts answering unready, so a load balancer in front of it stops sending new connections. Sessions already open keep running. `POST /fleet/instances/{instance}/undrain` reverses it.

The call goes to that one instance and its answer (status, headers and body) is passed back unchanged. `404` here means the aggregator does not know the instance; `502` that it could not reach it or could not read its answer (an answer over 8 MiB is refused).

parameters.name: instance

parameters.description: Who is acting. The console sets it to the signed-in user on a write; it is logged and passed on to each instance, and nothing else reads it.
parameters.name: X-Actor

200.description: The instance's own answer, passed through.

404.description: No instance of that name has pushed.

502.description: The instance could not be reached or its answer could not be read.

A node is `stale` after 30 seconds without a push, `degraded` when it pushes and at least one backend is unhealthy, and `ok` otherwise. Region and tags are what an instance reports about itself (`--region`, `--tag key=value`); the aggregator stores nothing of its own. Query keys it does not know are ignored.

get.description: Fleet-wide rates and gauges per minute, from a rolling history of about an hour that every push feeds. Proxies push cumulative counters; the aggregator turns the differences into rates. A counter that went down means the instance restarted. A gap between pushes spreads the increase over the minutes it spans, so a silent instance never shows as a spike. There is no per-node series: only the fleet total and the series per listener, pool and region. The history is in memory: a restart of the aggregator starts the charts empty.

parameters.description: How far back to look: `5m`, `15m` (the default) or `1h`.
parameters.name: range

200.description: The series.

400.description: `range` is not one of the three values.

get.description: A server-sent-event stream of the merged fleet state: every instance with its pools, sessions, version, protocol, config revision and skew. The first event is the current view; another follows every accepted push, debounced by 150 ms so a burst of pushes lands as one event. There is no replay: a subscriber that falls behind just gets the current view next. Each event's `data` is a JSON array of the objects below. A reverse proxy in front of this route must not buffer the response and must allow a long read timeout.

200.description: The event stream; each event's data is a JSON array.

get.description: Answers `ok` while the process is up. It needs no token, so a probe can reach it. It is the aggregator's own liveness, not the fleet's: `GET /fleet/healthz` says when each instance was last heard from.

200.description: The text `ok`.

post.description:
A proxy reports a summary of itself: its pools and backends, session counts, listener counters and feature flags. The aggregator keeps the newest push per `instance` and overwrites it on the next one, in memory only. Proxies push every `--aggregator-interval-sec` seconds (default 10), and the aggregator calls an instance `stale` after 30 seconds of silence.

This route takes the **ingest token** (`--ingest-token`), not the admin token, and is gated on the `x-wayhouse-protocol` header: a caller on another protocol major, or with no header, gets `426`. The `admin_url` is checked against `--instance-url-allow`: the aggregator later sends the instance token to that URL, so a push may not name an arbitrary host.

parameters.description: The caller's wire protocol, `major.minor`.
parameters.name: x-wayhouse-protocol

200.description: Stored.

400.description: The instance name is empty, `admin_url` is not allowed, a field or list is over its limit, or the body is not JSON. (A body that is not JSON at all is answered with plain text.)

401.description: No bearer token, or the wrong one. Body: `unauthorized`.

422.description: The body is JSON but does not have the payload's shape.

426.description: The caller's protocol major differs, or the header is missing or unparsable. The body names both versions.

503.description: The store holds the most live instances it will take (10,000); this push is refused.

get.description: The aggregator's metrics in the Prometheus text format. `--metrics-token-file` names a token that unlocks only this route, so a scraper need not hold the admin token; without it the admin token is required.

200.description: Prometheus text format.
